instructions: Add one confirmed row per concrete evidence item. Cite canonical source files, copy verifier excerpts verbatim, and judge source presence separately from recovery.

criteria.criterion: Access Open Library edition via ISBN-13 (9780141439518)
criteria.description: Attempt to open Open Library using the ISBN route (e.g., /isbn/9780141439518) or otherwise demonstrate that the viewed edition page is the one resolved from the supplied ISBN (starting URL context is acceptable if it corresponds to that resolved edition). Full credit if the agent attempts this but Open Library is inaccessible (down/CAPTCHA/rate-limited) and the agent clearly reports the blocking issue. Partial credit if the agent reaches the correct work but it is unclear whether the edition is ISBN-resolved. No credit if the agent clearly uses a different edition than the one resolved from the supplied ISBN when the ISBN-resolved page is accessible.

screenshot_context.verifier_evidence: Action history shows the agent started on https://openlibrary.org/books/OL37076991M/Pride_and_Prejudice (edition page) and only performed a scroll. Neither screenshot shows a URL bar or an /isbn/9780141439518 route, and no ISBN value is visible in either screenshot to directly tie the viewed page to the supplied ISBN. Latest screenshot (2) still does not display the ISBN or /isbn route.
screenshot_context.verifier_justification: The evidence supports that the agent accessed an Open Library edition page, but does not verify it was reached via ISBN resolution (or that the specific edition is the ISBN-resolved one). Because the action history does not include an /isbn/ lookup and screenshots don’t show the ISBN, keep partial credit rather than full.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: The browser shows an Open Library edition page with the header “OPEN LIBRARY” and the title area reading “An edition of Pride and Prejudice (1813)” and “Pride and Prejudice”. evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: Partial at best: the screenshot confirms the agent is on an Open Library edition page for “Pride and Prejudice,” but it does not provide visual confirmation that this edition was reached via the ISBN-13 route (9780141439518) or that it is the ISBN-resolved edition. Without the URL bar or an ISBN field visible, the ISBN-resolution requirement is not verifiable from the screenshot alone.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: Agent claims the edition is resolved via ISBN 9780141439518, but the screenshot provides no visible ISBN and no visible /isbn/ route or other explicit evidence of ISBN resolution.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: The screenshot shows an Open Library work/editions interface for “Pride and Prejudice.” At the top are tabs: “Overview” (selected), “View 4041 Editions,” “Details,” “12 Reviews,” “Lists,” and “Related Books.” Below, there is a table showing featured editions with an entry “Pride and Prejudice — 2003, Penguin Books — Paperback in English - Tanner introduction (3)” and two LibriVox audiobook entries. There is no visible URL bar and no visible text indicating navigation to an ISBN route like “/isbn/9780141439518,” nor any visible ISBN value on screen.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: The screenshot confirms the user is on an Open Library page for “Pride and Prejudice” and can see a 2003 Penguin Books edition in the featured editions list, but it does not demonstrate that the page/edition was accessed via the supplied ISBN-13 (9780141439518) or via an ISBN-resolved route. Since the screenshot lacks any visible ISBN resolution evidence (no URL, no ISBN field, no edition identifiers shown), this is at best partial support for Criterion 0.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: Agent’s predicted output states the edition was resolved via ISBN 9780141439518 and references fields like “Edition Identifiers → ISBN 13,” but the screenshot does not show any ISBN identifiers section, any ISBN number, or evidence of opening via /isbn/9780141439518.

dom_model_context.verifier_evidence: DOM-model state 1 (latest) shows the edition page https://openlibrary.org/books/OL37076991M/Pride_and_Prejudice. In Book Details → Edition Identifiers it explicitly lists “ISBN 13 9780141439518,” and the editions table row also includes “9780141439518.” There is no DOM evidence of using an /isbn/9780141439518 resolver route; Action History shows only a scroll on the edition URL.
dom_model_context.verifier_justification: The task requires using the edition resolved from the supplied ISBN. While the agent did not demonstrate an ISBN-resolver navigation step, the latest DOM explicitly confirms the currently viewed edition (OL37076991M) carries ISBN-13 9780141439518, which is strong confirmation that this is the ISBN-matched/resolved edition. Given the starting URL context note and explicit on-page ISBN match, keep full credit.

evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis:
EVIDENCE_STATUS: PARTIAL
The DOM confirms the viewed edition page (OL37076991M) has ISBN-13 9780141439518 in the Edition Identifiers section, which strongly suggests it corresponds to the supplied ISBN. However, there is no evidence in the DOM that the agent navigated via an ISBN resolver route (e.g., /isbn/9780141439518) or otherwise demonstrated resolution by ISBN; the URL shown is the edition URL.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: Criterion prefers evidence of ISBN-route resolution; DOM only shows the edition page contains the ISBN-13, not that it was reached through /isbn/9780141439518.

criteria.criterion: Follow constraints (no sign-in/borrow/waitlist; stop after fields captured)
criteria.description: Do not sign in, borrow, or join a waitlist. Stop once all requested fields have been recorded (or explicitly marked unavailable on the ISBN-resolved edition page). Full credit if constraints are respected. Partial credit if there is unnecessary navigation that does not violate constraints. No credit if the agent signs in, borrows, or joins a waitlist.

screenshot_context.verifier_evidence: Screenshots show Log In/Sign Up buttons (not signed in) and no borrow/join waitlist actions. Action history only includes a scroll.
screenshot_context.verifier_justification: No constraint violations are evidenced (no sign-in/borrow/waitlist). The agent appears to have stopped after compiling fields (even though ISBN-13 display is unverified). Keep full credit for following constraints.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: Top right shows “Log In” and “Sign Up” buttons, indicating the user is not signed in. evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis: Satisfied regarding constraints: there is no evidence of signing in, borrowing, or joining a waitlist in the screenshot. The page indicates unavailability and only a preview, which aligns with not borrowing. The stopping condition cannot be fully assessed from the screenshot alone, but the visible behavior does not violate constraints.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: None indicating a constraint violation. The screenshot shows an “unavailable” notice and login/signup options, but no evidence the agent used them.

dom_model_context.verifier_evidence: Action History shows only a scroll action. DOM-model states show login/availability messaging but no evidence of signing in, borrowing, or joining a waitlist. Agent output includes all requested fields and stops.
dom_model_context.verifier_justification: No prohibited actions are evidenced, and the response stops after providing the requested metadata. Keep full credit.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX: 1 shows no sign-in flow and indicates “Preview Only” / “Search Only a preview is available.” Action history includes only a scroll action. evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis:
EVIDENCE_STATUS: PARTIAL
No evidence of signing in, borrowing, or joining a waitlist; only scrolling occurred, consistent with constraints. However, the stopping condition/field completeness is not fully supported by DOM because some requested fields are not evidenced in this snapshot: Publish Date is shown as “Copyright Date 2003” (not explicitly labeled “Publish Date” in the visible DOM), and publisher/language are not shown in the Book Details text captured here (they may exist elsewhere but are not present in the provided DOM excerpt). Thus, we cannot confirm all requested fields were recorded from the ISBN-resolved edition without substitution.
evidence_analyses.discrepancies: Agent reported “Publisher: Penguin Books” and “Language: English” but these are not explicitly present in the captured Book Details block; only the editions table row text includes “2003, Penguin Books … in English,” which is partial support but not clearly a dedicated publisher/language field. Publish Date was reported as 2003 based on “Copyright Date 2003,” which is not the same label as “Publish Date” in the DOM.

evidence_analyses.screenshot_evidence: DOM_MODEL_STATE_INDEX: 0 shows “Log In” / “Sign Up” options and mentions “Only a preview is available.” and “This book is currently unavailable on Open Library...”. Action history shows only a scroll action (Action 1: scroll pixels 800). No evidence of clicking “Borrow”, signing in, or joining a waitlist.
evidence_analyses.criterion_analysis:

Within the provided evidence, the agent did not sign in, borrow, or join a waitlist (only scrolled). The agent’s predicted output stops after reporting the requested fields. Note: the constraint “Use the edition reached through the supplied ISBN” cannot be verified from this DOM snapshot because the ISBN is not shown, but the non-borrow/non-sign-in/stop behavior is supported.
